title: Invited: Graph Learning for Parameter Prediction of Quantum Approximate Optimization Algorithm
problem: QAOA parameter initialization requires optimization to reduce quantum computational resource overhead. Current quantum systems face severe resource constraints that limit practical application on combinatorial problems like Max-Cut.
motivation: Quantum computing resource limitations hinder practical deployment of QAOA algorithms for real-world combinatorial optimization problems.
method: Uses Graph Neural Networks as a warm-start technique for QAOA parameter initialization, evaluating multiple GNN architectures. The approach trades classical computational resources for reduced quantum resource requirements during algorithm execution.
key_novelty: GNN-based parameter warm-starting for QAOA to reduce quantum resource overhead through classical preprocessing.
contributions: GNN-based warm-start mechanism for QAOA parameter initialization
Experimental validation of GNN adaptability across different architectures
Framework reducing quantum computational resource overhead
Demonstration of hybrid quantum-classical optimization synergy
limitations: Scalability analysis, convergence guarantees, and practical feasibility on current quantum hardware not discussed.
primary_theme: Hybrid quantum-classical optimization via GNN parameter prediction
